en: Mount Pulag, not Mount Apo, is the highest mountain in the Luzon island group, reaching an elevation of 2,928 meters above sea level.
Unlike flat-topped volcanoes, Mayon Volcano in Albay is globally famous for its perfectly symmetrical, steep conical shape formed by repeated historical eruptions.
The Cagayan River, rather than the shorter Pasig River, holds the title of the longest and largest river in the entire Philippine archipelago.
The famous Chocolate Hills of Bohol are actually composed of marine limestone and clay formations that turn brown only during the dry season.
Laguna de Bay is a large freshwater lake formed by volcanic and tectonic processes, not by a meteorite impact crater.
Taal Volcano is uniquely situated on Volcano Island, which is an island located entirely within Taal Lake in the province of Batangas.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo actually destroyed its summit, lowering its elevation and leaving behind a large, water-filled caldera.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is not located near the shore, but sits 150 kilometers offshore in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
Mount Halcon is not located in Mindanao, but is actually the highest peak on the island of Mindoro within the Luzon island group.
Although broadly described as having two seasons, the Philippine dry season is officially subdivided into the cool dry period and the hot dry period.
The Chico River in the Cordillera region flows northwest to join the Cagayan River, eventually emptying into the Luzon Strait, not the Pacific Ocean.
The Visayas is not a single landmass, but a geographical division consisting of several major islands, including Panay, Negros, Cebu, Bohol, and Leyte.
